content: The following studies and declarations provide insights into the transmission of hepatitis C virus (HCV), particularly among HIV-positive men who have sex with men (MSM), as well as the involvement of various experts in the development of related guidelines: 1. Browne et al. (2004) reported an increase in acute hepatitis C infections among HIV-positive homosexual men, raising the question of whether sexual transmission is contributing to this rise. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections (Volume 80, Issue 4, Pages 326–327). 2. Terrault (2005) explored the relationship between sexual activity and hepatitis C in an article published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology (Volume 100, Issue 4, Pages 825–826). 3. Hagan et al. (2015) investigated the incidence of sexually transmitted HCV infections in HIV-positive MSM. Their findings were published in AIDS (Volume 29, Issue 17, Pages 2335–2345). 4. Vanhommerig et al. (2015) conducted a case-control study to identify risk factors for the sexual transmission of HCV among HIV-infected MSM. This research was published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases (Volume 2, Issue 3, Article ofv115). 5. Hoornenborg et al. This study was published in AIDS (Volume 31, Issue 11, Pages 1603–1610).
